title: A Summer in the Azores, with a Glimpse of Madeira
publisher: Lee and Shepard; Charles T. Dillingham

divisions.title: The book’s title above the first chapter

summary: A diary of a summer’s holiday in the Azores, written by a teacher from Cambridge, Massachusetts, who sails from Boston with a small party of friends on a bark bound for Fayal. The chapters, each headed with a date, describe the voyage, with a whaling captain’s story told in his own words; the port of Horta and its streets, donkeys, and peasant life; the Caldeira of Fayal and the peak of Pico; a passing look at San Jorge, Graciosa, and Terceira; and San Miguel, where the party stays in the valley of the Furnas, with its hot springs, and goes to a ball.
A short visit to Madeira follows: a stay in quarantine off Funchal, then rides in bullock-sledges and on horseback. The party goes home by way of the Azores.
notes_on_text: The book gives no year for the journey. The dates at the heads of the chapters run from June to September; the days of the week fit 1873 or 1879.
